rv.q: Mar a Irene Forn s's ingenious Fefu and Her Friends is such a work, and this revival from director Lileana Blain-Cruz is nothing short of exquisite.
It’s a strong and necessary production.
And a good revival it is — I think; it seems well acted and designed.
Four decades after it debuted, Fefu still hits us like a shot between the eyes.

A blast for much of the time. For the rest…well, to quote the director. 'Oh my god. I don't understand anything that's going on, but I love it.'…a pioneer in immersive theater decades before the term was in use.

While María Irene Fornés’ Fefu and Her Friends is considered a feminist statement, in performance the play seems not to be very revealing about women or their positions other than the fact that the cast is entirely female.
Fefu and Her Friends is an absorbing and thoughtful, if somewhat enigmatic, work that is distinguished by its unorthodox structure.
